findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the intent-journal crash-recovery contract (lifecycle, the three discrimination states, and the invariant that SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT carries NO journal so fsck stays its sole owner) in an ADR or design-doc/AGENTS.md, not only in child-decomposition prose.
evidence: Plan: 'Discrimination of the two half-fold states is by an INTENT JOURNAL (a commit-pending sentinel) ... the retained SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT state has NO journal by construction, so the preamble never touches it — fsck --repair-snapshots remains its sole owner.'
The journal is written by compaction, read by the recovery preamble, and its absence is load-bearing for fsck's ownership of SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT — a multi-owner invariant that lives only in prose.
T5e documentation sub-check: a novel architectural decision should be captured in an ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a novel crash-recovery contract — the INTENT JOURNAL (commit-pending sentinel under the tracker git dir) with a three-state discrimination machine spanning compaction (writer), the sync recovery preamble (reader/reverter), and fsck (sole owner of the no-journal SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT state). This is a new cross-component pattern whose correctness depends on all three owners agreeing on the journal lifecycle, but the plan captures it only in child-decomposition prose and names no ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc artifact where the contract is durably recorded for future maintainers.
findings.location: Child decomposition -> 'Crash-atomic compaction fold ... Discrimination of the two half-fold states is by an INTENT JOURNAL'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile c925's tracker-dirty fsck detection with bb80's active-only default scan: state whether dirty-tree/leftover/lock detection is whole-tree (scope-independent) or subject to `--include-archived`, so a dirty archived ticket dir is not silently hidden from default `rebar fsck`.
evidence: bb80 approach: 'Switch the fsck scan loops to it' (active-only iterator) and 'Default = active-only for both'; scope edits 'src/rebar/_commands/fsck_scan.py — scan loops take the shared active-only iterator'.

c925 scope edits 'src/rebar/_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py — tracker-dirty classification' and classifies untracked regenerable leftovers (`*-SNAPSHOT.json`, `*.retired`) and orphaned locks per ticket dir, but does not state whether its scan honors or bypasses the active-only default.

Both children edit the fsck surface but neither names the other; c925 targets fsck_tracker_health.py / fsck.py while bb80 targets fsck_scan.py — the coupling between the per-ticket-dir walk and the tracker-dirty classification is unspecified.
findings.finding: bb80 flips the DEFAULT fsck scan to active-only (skipping archived ticket dirs), while c925 adds tracker-dirty classification to the fsck scan surface; the two children do not reconcile whether c925's new dirty-tree/leftover detection is subject to bb80's active-only default, risking a dirty archived ticket dir being invisible to default `rebar fsck`.
findings.location: child c925-7669-ded8-43a3 (fsck tracker-dirty detection) vs child bb80-80d0-5f6b-4d45 (active-only default scan scoping)
scenarios: An archived ticket dir retains untracked compaction leftovers (*.retired / *-SNAPSHOT.json) after an interrupted fold; if c925's leftover detection walks via bb80's active-only iterator, default `rebar fsck` skips that archived dir and never reports the dirt, requiring the operator to remember `--include-archived` for a wedge-class finding.

Conversely, if c925's tracker-dirty check reads whole-tree `git status --porcelain` (not per-dir iteration), it may report findings in archived dirs that bb80's active-only counts intentionally exclude — an inconsistency in the same fsck run.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that c925's tracker-dirty classification runs against whole-tree `git status --porcelain` (independent of the active-only ticket-dir iterator), or explicitly document that leftover/lock findings in archived dirs require `--include-archived` and confirm the parent's detection contract still holds.
